page: OVHcloud b3-128-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform running under the KVM hypervisor. The configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz with one thread per core, avoiding virtual thread contention. Processor cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting standard instruction extensions including AVX, AES, and SHA_NI. The compute environment is paired with 128 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Bundled storage is limited to a 50 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate top-quartile execution across multi-core computing metrics. Stress-ng multi-core evaluations, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang software compilation tests achieve strong ratings. Memory throughput is particularly high for small-block cached reads, reflected in high in-memory transactional rates where Redis SET performance reaches 73.71 million operations per second. Conversely, single-thread performance metrics, including single-core Geekbench and gzip compression, reflect average performance bands. Large-block uncached memory read and write operations also track within midrange thresholds, pointing to optimal utilization when operations fit within CPU cache boundaries.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the dedicated physical core model delivers predictable performance without hyperthreading overhead. The 50 GB local NVMe storage provides rapid scratch execution, though larger applications require external block storage. With substantial memory capacity, reliable multi-threaded compute, and balanced networking throughput, this instance fits enterprise continuous integration pipelines, software compilation fleets, Redis caching layers, and production relational database workloads.
description: OVHcloud b3-128-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture running at 2.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 128 GB of memory, accompanied by 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network connection. The platform lacks GPU acceleration, targeting CPU-bound and memory-balanced tasks. Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded execution, highlighting superior throughput in software compilation, multi-core stress operations, and in-memory key-value processing where Redis SET tests exceed 73 million operations per second. However, single-core processing and large-block uncached memory transfers land within median industry percentiles. Offering complete physical core isolation and high memory density, this configuration is well aligned with parallel build systems, CI/CD automation, distributed caching, and mid-sized database management systems.
